PulseBrief's Update Pulse


as of Wed, Jun 17, 14:25


Cyber Security


30,000+ Fortinet Devices Compromised in Sweeping Credential-Harvesting Campaign


Jun 17, 24:00


Attackers have compiled working credentials for over 30,000 Fortinet devices across nearly 200 countries in an active credential-harvesting campaign targeting multiple sectors. The scale and geographic breadth make this one of the most significant Fortinet compromise events on record. Organizations running Fortinet infrastructure should treat credential rotation and access audits as immediate priorities.


30,000 compromised network security devices across 200 countries is a mass-scale enterprise infrastructure event with immediate incident response implications


Sources: Dark Reading


Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Added to CISA KEV — Actively Exploited in Ransomware Attacks


Jun 17, 24:00


CISA added CVE-2026-35273, a critical Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability classified as missing authentication for a critical function, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirming active exploitation in ransomware attacks. Unauthenticated attackers can gain full system control. Federal agencies face mandatory patch deadlines and all organizations running PeopleSoft should treat this as urgent.


A PeopleSoft zero-day being actively weaponized in ransomware attacks hits the HR and ERP backbone of large enterprises and government agencies directly


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Malicious JetBrains Marketplace Plugins With 70,000+ Installs Steal AI API Keys


Jun 17, 24:00


At least 15 malicious plugins downloaded over 70,000 times were discovered on the JetBrains Marketplace, all posing as AI coding assistants built on DeepSeek and other LLMs while exfiltrating API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI providers. Published under seven different vendor accounts, the coordinated campaign also extended to Chrome extensions capturing chatbot conversations. Developers should audit installed plugins immediately and rotate any exposed API keys.


70,000+ installs of AI API key-stealing plugins in the IDE developers use most is a direct, large-scale compromise of AI infrastructure credentials


Sources: The Hacker News · Cybersecurity News


Secure Boot Key Expiration Deadline Imminent for Windows and Linux Users


Jun 17, 24:00


A deadline is approaching for Windows and Linux users to update Secure Boot keys that secure their machine's boot sequence, with three sources flagging the urgency. Failing to update before expiration could leave systems vulnerable to boot-level attacks or unable to boot after future security updates. System administrators managing large fleets should prioritize this across all managed endpoints.


A missed Secure Boot key rotation deadline creates a silent, fleet-wide boot security gap that attackers can exploit for persistent low-level compromise


Sources: Ars Technica


Kodak Confirms Breach: ShinyHunters Claims 2.2 Million Customer Records Stolen


Jun 17, 24:00


Eastman Kodak confirmed unauthorized access to its systems after the ShinyHunters extortion group claimed to have stolen over 2.2 million records containing customer PII and internal corporate data. Kodak acknowledged an unauthorized third party 'briefly accessed a limited amount' of data. ShinyHunters has a consistent track record of following through on breach claims.


A confirmed breach with 2.2 million customer records claimed by one of the most prolific extortion groups signals high probability of eventual data exposure


Sources: Cybersecurity News


ErrTraffic Malware-as-a-Service Exploits Fake CAPTCHA and Cloudflare Turnstile to Run PowerShell


Jun 17, 24:00


A rapidly growing cybercrime framework called ErrTraffic tricks users into executing malicious PowerShell commands by impersonating legitimate reCAPTCHA and Cloudflare Turnstile verification screens. First appearing in late 2025, ErrTraffic is being offered as a Malware-as-a-Service platform, dramatically lowering the barrier to deploy this social engineering vector at scale. The lure exploits users' conditioned trust in CAPTCHA-style prompts.


A MaaS platform automating fake-CAPTCHA PowerShell execution attacks at scale is a direct escalation of one of the most effective current social engineering techniques


Sources: Cybersecurity News


AI & Machine Learning


Anthropic Employees Accuse Trump Administration of Targeting Them Personally


Jun 17, 24:00


Workers at Anthropic say they are puzzled and increasingly alarmed by the White House's move to restrict their Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models, with some believing the administration is targeting the company and its employees beyond normal regulatory action. The NYT report adds a human dimension to the ongoing standoff, suggesting the export control action is being experienced internally as politically motivated. The U.K. separately denied seeking a carve-out from the restrictions while signaling growing digital sovereignty concerns.


Internal Anthropic reaction to the ban and UK diplomatic positioning are key signals of how the Anthropic-White House standoff is escalating — with direct enterprise AI vendor risk implications


Sources: New York Times · Politico EU


U.S. Commerce Department Formally Imposes Export Controls on Claude Mythos 5 and Fable 5


Jun 17, 24:00


The Bureau of Industry and Security issued an 'Is Informed' letter to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei mandating that the company obtain an individually validated export license before sharing Claude Mythos 5 and Fable 5 with any foreign national anywhere in the world. This is the formal legal instrument behind the widely reported ban, representing a landmark use of export control authority against an AI model. The requirement applies globally, not just to specific countries.


The formal BIS legal instrument is the clearest articulation yet of how U.S. export control law is being applied to frontier AI models — setting precedent for every AI vendor and enterprise buyer


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Pramaana Labs Raises $27M from Khosla to Bring Formal Verification to AI


Jun 17, 24:00


Pramaana Labs emerged with a $27 million seed round from Khosla Ventures to apply formal verification methods to AI outputs in high-stakes domains including law, drug discovery, and tax preparation. The startup's approach aims to provide mathematical guarantees of correctness rather than probabilistic accuracy — directly addressing the reliability gap that has blocked AI adoption in regulated industries. Formal verification is borrowed from hardware design and safety-critical software engineering.


Formal verification for AI in law, pharma, and tax directly addresses the enterprise reliability barrier that has kept AI out of high-consequence professional workflows


Sources: TechCrunch


Meta Launches AI Mode in Facebook Search, Drawing on Public Posts Across Meta Apps


Jun 17, 24:00


Meta has launched 'AI Mode' as a new search option in the Facebook app, designed to handle complex conversational queries by drawing on public posts across Facebook Groups, Instagram Reels, and other Meta platforms. The feature competes directly with Google's AI Mode in Search but uses Meta's unique social content corpus. Early hands-on coverage notes accuracy problems, with the system prone to errors grounded in unreliable user-generated content.


AI search grounded in Facebook posts introduces a new reliability risk profile — and signals Meta's intent to compete directly with Google for AI-powered information retrieval at scale


Sources: The Verge


Waymo's Nationwide Autonomous Taxi Rollout Hits Political Roadblocks in Major Markets


Jun 17, 24:00


The New York Times reports that Waymo's ambitions to expand driverless taxis nationally are being blocked by political opposition in several of the country's largest markets, despite strong performance data in existing deployments. Local regulatory resistance, labor concerns from taxi and rideshare unions, and municipal politics are combining to slow expansion well beyond what technical readiness would warrant. The dynamic illustrates how political and regulatory friction — not technology — is now the primary constraint on autonomous vehicle deployment.


The gap between Waymo's technical capability and its deployment pace due to political friction is a critical signal for enterprise planning around autonomous vehicle timelines


Sources: New York Times


Technology


Google Home Speaker Launches June 29 — First New Google Smart Speaker in Six Years


Jun 17, 24:00


Google's first new smart speaker since 2020 begins shipping June 29th, priced at $99 and built around Gemini for Home rather than Google Assistant. Preorders opened today in four colors, with the device featuring a redesigned round form factor and a light ring status indicator. The six-year gap reflects Google's pivot from hardware experimentation to Gemini-first smart home strategy.


Google's return to smart speaker hardware after six years marks a Gemini-native inflection point for the smart home platform — directly affects enterprise and consumer IoT ecosystem decisions


Sources: The Verge · Wired


UK Competition Authority Orders Google to Make Search Rankings Transparent


Jun 17, 24:00


The UK's Competition and Markets Authority has ordered Google to make its search ranking criteria less opaque, with new rules covering organic rankings, AI Overviews, and user-approved search data sharing. The order follows the CMA's ongoing investigation into Google's search dominance and represents one of the most concrete regulatory interventions into algorithmic transparency in the UK to date. The rules will affect how SEO, content, and AI-generated summaries interact with Google's ranking systems.


Mandatory search ranking transparency from a major regulator reshapes SEO strategy, AI Overview optimization, and enterprise content visibility planning in the UK market


Sources: The Register


RFC 10008 Published: HTTP Gets an Official QUERY Method


Jun 17, 24:00


RFC 10008 has been published, officially defining a new HTTP QUERY method designed for safe, idempotent requests that carry a request body — filling a long-standing gap where developers had to misuse POST for structured queries. The new method is semantically closer to GET but allows complex query payloads, addressing a core limitation in REST API design. It garnered 127 upvotes and 66 comments on Hacker News, signaling strong developer interest.


A new official HTTP method is a foundational web standards change that affects API design, caching infrastructure, and every web framework — developers need to know it exists


Sources: IETF RFC Editor


Intel Begins Production of Enhanced 18A-P Process Node with 9% Speed Boost


Jun 17, 24:00


Intel has started manufacturing silicon on its enhanced 18A-P process node, which the company claims delivers a 9% performance improvement over standard 18A without additional power draw and maintains design compatibility. The 18A-P ramp is aimed at attracting foundry customers who want a performance uplift path without re-taping out designs. The development is a critical milestone for Intel Foundry's competitiveness against TSMC's N2 process.


Intel Foundry's ability to offer a performance-enhanced node compatible with existing 18A designs is a key signal of whether it can realistically compete for advanced semiconductor manufacturing contracts


Sources: The Register


Microsoft Confirms June Windows Update Breaks Third-Party Office Document Launches


Jun 17, 24:00


Microsoft is investigating a bug introduced by June's Windows updates that prevents third-party applications from launching Microsoft Office apps or opening documents, affecting up-to-date Windows systems. The issue impacts workflows where applications use OLE to trigger Office document handling — a deeply embedded enterprise integration pattern. No fix has shipped yet, leaving organizations dependent on these integrations with broken document launch workflows.


A Windows update breaking Office document launch from third-party apps is an immediate enterprise productivity disruption affecting standard business workflows across Microsoft-dependent organizations


Sources: BleepingComputer · The Register


Business & Markets


SpaceX's War Chest Grows as Stock Surge Gives Musk Financial Resources to Box Out Competitors


Jun 17, 24:00


SpaceX shares continue surging, with the NYT DealBook analysis noting the company now has an unprecedented financial war chest from its $2.6–2.7 trillion market cap to fund acquisitions and outcompete rivals in AI, launch, and defense. The Cursor acquisition at $60 billion in all-stock was executed with essentially no cash outlay. Elon Musk is now confirmed as the world's first trillionaire.


SpaceX's ability to make $60B acquisitions in stock with no cash impact redefines competitive dynamics in AI software, cloud, and defense contracting — every enterprise in those markets is now competing against a near-unlimited balance sheet


Sources: New York Times DealBook


Oil Prices Rise as U.S.-Iran Cease-Fire Talks in Switzerland Could Reopen Strait of Hormuz


Jun 17, 24:00


Oil prices ticked higher on reports that U.S. and Iranian officials are expected to meet in Switzerland on Friday to sign an initial agreement and begin a 60-day cease-fire, which would pave the way for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Markets are pricing in a significant reduction in the energy supply disruption that has driven post-war inflation. The outcome of Friday's talks will directly affect global energy costs and the Fed's inflation calculus.


A Strait of Hormuz reopening would be the single largest near-term positive shock to global energy prices and supply chains — directly affecting enterprise cost structures across every industry


Sources: New York Times


1Password Acquires Apono for Reported $250M–$300M to Add JIT Access Governance for AI Agents


Jun 17, 24:00


1Password has acquired Apono, a just-in-time access governance platform for humans, machines, and AI agents, in a deal reported at $250–300 million. The acquisition extends 1Password's credential management platform into dynamic, time-limited access provisioning — a critical capability as AI agents increasingly need controlled access to enterprise systems. The deal signals that identity and access management vendors are racing to cover the AI agent attack surface.


A $250–300M acquisition specifically targeting JIT access governance for AI agents confirms that securing agentic AI infrastructure is now a funded, competitive market segment


Sources: SecurityWeek


BMW Warns of 'Significant' 2026 Profit Decline as China Sales Slump and Energy Costs Bite


Jun 17, 24:00


BMW issued a profit warning for 2026, citing a combination of weak Chinese sales — where the company faces intensifying competition from domestic EV makers — and elevated energy costs stemming from Middle East conflict disruption. Shares fell 7% on the announcement. The warning is a bellwether for European luxury manufacturing's exposure to the dual pressures of China market share erosion and post-war energy economics.


BMW's profit warning reflects structural pressures — China EV competition and energy cost inflation — that are simultaneously hitting multiple large European industrial companies and supply chains


Sources: Euronews Business


Canadian Pension Giant Acquires 8.2% Stake in India's CtrlS Data Center Operator


Jun 17, 24:00


A major Canadian pension fund is acquiring an 8.2% stake in CtrlS, which operates over 15 data centers across India, joining a wave of institutional capital targeting India's AI-fueled data center buildout. India has emerged as a key destination for AI infrastructure investment as U.S.-China tensions reshape where global compute capacity gets built. The pension fund entry signals the data center investment wave has moved well beyond venture and tech-sector capital.


Pension fund capital entering India's data center market confirms the AI infrastructure buildout has become a mainstream institutional asset class with multi-decade return horizons


Sources: TechCrunch


Warner Warns of CISA Staffing Gaps as Agency Faces Budget Cuts


Jun 17, 24:00


Senator Mark Warner sent letters to both CISA's acting chief and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin warning of staffing shortages and budget cuts undermining the agency's ability to fulfill its cybersecurity mission, including funding for the MS-ISAC information sharing program. The warning comes as CISA manages an active threat landscape including multiple KEV additions and supply chain attacks. Cuts to CISA directly reduce the threat intelligence and coordination infrastructure that enterprises rely on.


CISA budget and staffing degradation weakens the government cybersecurity backstop that enterprises and critical infrastructure operators depend on for threat intelligence and incident coordination


Sources: The Record

PulseBrief's Update Pulse


as of Wed, Jun 17, 09:27


Cyber Security


144 Mastra npm Packages Compromised in Supply Chain Attack Targeting AI Developers


Jun 17, 07:38


A hijacked contributor account (ehindero) was used to mass-publish malicious versions of 144 packages in the @mastra/* npm namespace — a popular JS/TS framework for building AI applications — deploying infostealer malware on developer machines, CI/CD runners, and build environments. The campaign, dubbed 'easy-day-js,' was independently flagged by JFrog, SafeDep, Socket, StepSecurity, and Microsoft. Any organization using Mastra for AI agent development should audit dependencies and rotate secrets immediately.


A supply chain attack specifically targeting the AI development toolchain hits developers building the next generation of AI systems — stolen credentials and API keys from build environments have outsized downstream blast radius


Sources: The Hacker News · Cybersecurity News


GitHub Dismissed Vulnerability Reports Now Enabling Shai-Hulud Supply-Chain Worm


Jun 16, 23:00


Researchers say GitHub rejected two formal vulnerability disclosures identifying design flaws that are now being actively exploited by variants of the Shai-Hulud supply-chain worm, which is spreading across hundreds of software packages and developer accounts globally. GitHub's decision not to act on the reports is drawing significant criticism as the worm's spread widens. The incident raises urgent questions about how platform owners handle reports of systemic design-level vulnerabilities versus discrete CVEs.


A platform the size of GitHub dismissing reports that enabled a live, spreading supply-chain worm is a critical failure with industry-wide consequences for open source software integrity


Sources: The Record


Microsoft Defender Zero-Day 'RoguePlanet' Still Unpatched One Week After Disclosure


Jun 17, 08:32


Microsoft confirmed it is working on a patch for a Defender zero-day named 'RoguePlanet,' disclosed a week ago, with no fix yet available. The vulnerability sits in one of the most widely deployed endpoint security products in enterprise environments globally. Until a patch ships, organizations running Defender have no vendor-supplied mitigation for an actively disclosed flaw.


An unpatched zero-day in the world's most widely deployed endpoint security product is a direct, unresolved exposure for the majority of enterprise Windows environments


Sources: BleepingComputer


CISA Adds Maximum-Severity Joomla JCE Flaw (CVSS 10.0) to KEV — Active Exploitation Underway


Jun 17, 05:50


CISA added CVE-2026-48907, a CVSS 10.0 improper access control flaw in the widely used JetBrains JCE Joomla plugin, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirming active exploitation enabling arbitrary PHP code execution. Simultaneously, the previously reported LiteSpeed cPanel root-escalation zero-day also remains under active attack. Federal agencies have mandatory patch deadlines; all Joomla-based web infrastructure should be treated as urgent.


A perfect-10 CVSS flaw being actively exploited in one of the web's most common CMS plugin ecosystems is a broad and immediate threat to web infrastructure


Sources: The Hacker News · SecurityWeek


Malicious JetBrains Marketplace Plugins Caught Stealing AI API Keys from Developers


Jun 16, 21:54


At least 15 malicious plugins discovered on the JetBrains Marketplace were specifically engineered to exfiltrate AI API keys — targeting developers' credentials for OpenAI, Anthropic, and other providers stored in IDE configurations. JetBrains IDEs are used by tens of millions of developers worldwide, making the marketplace a high-value supply chain target. Developers should audit installed plugins and rotate any API keys that may have been exposed.


AI API key theft from developer tooling directly enables attackers to hijack AI infrastructure, run up costs, and access proprietary model interactions at the victim's expense


Sources: BleepingComputer


Chrome and Firefox Both Updated for Critical Memory Safety RCE Vulnerabilities


Jun 17, 08:21


Google and Mozilla released back-to-back updates patching critical and high-severity memory safety bugs in Chrome and Firefox respectively, with several flaws carrying remote code execution potential. Chrome stable was updated to version 149.0.7827.155/156. Both browsers are ubiquitous across enterprise environments, making prompt update enforcement a near-universal IT action item.


Simultaneous critical RCE patches for the two dominant browsers represent a mandatory, time-sensitive update cycle for every enterprise endpoint management program


Sources: SecurityWeek · Cybersecurity News


Hackers Actively Using Claude and OpenAI Codex for Reconnaissance, Exploitation, and Data Exfiltration


Jun 17, 06:36


Security researchers documented real-world attacks where threat actors are using Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's Codex agents as full operational tools — automating multi-stage intrusions including reconnaissance, exploitation, and data exfiltration while disguising activity as 'authorized red team' work to evade detection. The AI coding assistants dramatically lower the skill barrier for complex attacks. The report directly validates the core concern behind the White House's Anthropic model restrictions.


Documented in-the-wild weaponization of frontier AI coding agents for intrusion operations is the most concrete evidence yet of the offensive capability risks driving the Anthropic ban debate


Sources: Cybersecurity News


AI & Machine Learning


Security Community Publishes Open Letter Demanding Reversal of Anthropic Fable 5 / Mythos 5 Ban


Jun 16, 22:00


Dozens of security researchers and experts signed an open letter calling on the White House to reverse its emergency export control order banning Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models, arguing the ban is counterproductive and sets a dangerous precedent for AI governance. The letter comes as Anthropic remains at an impasse with the administration and new evidence shows threat actors are already using existing AI tools offensively regardless of the restrictions. The security community's unified pushback represents the clearest expert signal yet that the policy is viewed as technically incoherent.


Expert consensus opposing the ban shapes the political and regulatory trajectory of AI export control policy — a key signal for enterprises navigating AI vendor risk


Sources: Dark Reading


Anthropic's White House Feud May Be Boosting Enterprise Sales, Spending Data Suggests


Jun 16, 22:34


Corporate card spending data from Ramp shows Anthropic's popularity with business users has been growing strongly, with the government standoff potentially acting as a marketing signal of capability rather than a deterrent. Enterprise buyers appear to be interpreting the ban on Fable 5 and Mythos 5 as validation of the models' power rather than a reason to avoid the platform. The counterintuitive commercial dynamic complicates the White House's leverage in the ongoing negotiation.


If the ban is driving enterprise adoption rather than suppressing it, the policy calculus changes significantly — directly relevant to enterprise AI vendor selection and competitive positioning


Sources: TechCrunch


Anthropic Publishes 'Founder's Playbook' for AI-Native Startups — Gaining Significant Traction


Jun 17, 07:04


Anthropic published a detailed 'Founder's Playbook' on the Claude blog aimed at entrepreneurs building AI-native companies, drawing 66 upvotes and 71 comments on Hacker News within hours. The post covers architecture, product strategy, and go-to-market frameworks specific to AI-native business models. The timing — during the Fable 5 ban controversy — signals Anthropic is actively expanding its developer and founder ecosystem even amid regulatory pressure.


Direct Anthropic vendor content signaling strategic priorities during a politically turbulent period; the HN traction confirms developer community interest


Sources: Anthropic / Claude Blog


Weibo's VibeThinker-3B Claims to Match 671B-Parameter Models on AIME 2026 — Benchmark Credibility Under Fire


Jun 17, 24:32


Researchers at Sina Weibo published VibeThinker-3B, a 3-billion parameter model claiming a 94.3 score on AIME 2026 — matching DeepSeek V3.2 (671B parameters) and beating Gemini 3 Pro — using a test-time scaling technique called Claim-Level Reliability Assessment. The paper generated over 161,000 views on X and 685 GitHub stars within hours, but also intense skepticism about whether AI benchmarks have become so gameable they've lost meaning. The story cuts to the core tension between genuine efficiency breakthroughs and benchmark manipulation in the AI race.


If a 3B model genuinely matches 671B models on hard reasoning tasks, it reshapes cost/capability tradeoffs for enterprise AI; if the benchmarks are broken, the entire industry's evaluation framework is in question


Sources: VentureBeat


Z.ai Releases GLM-5.2: Open-Weights 753B Model Beating GPT-5.5 on Long-Horizon Coding at 1/6th the Cost


Jun 16, 21:26


Chinese AI startup Z.ai (formerly Zhipu AI) released GLM-5.2, a 753-billion parameter open-weights model under an MIT license that outperforms GPT-5.5 on multiple long-horizon coding benchmarks with a 1-million token context window and enterprise tiers starting at $12.60/month. The model is available now on Hugging Face for self-hosting. The release directly capitalizes on enterprise anxiety over U.S. AI export controls, offering a locally-hostable frontier model that bypasses geographic restrictions entirely.


An MIT-licensed, self-hostable model that beats GPT-5.5 on coding benchmarks is a concrete alternative for enterprises seeking to avoid U.S. regulatory exposure — the export control crisis is accelerating open-weights adoption


Sources: VentureBeat


Wolfram Language and Mathematica Version 15 Launches with Built-In AI


Jun 16, 23:15


Stephen Wolfram announced the release of Wolfram Language and Mathematica version 15, featuring built-in AI capabilities integrated directly into the computational notebook environment, drawing 163 upvotes and 78 comments on Hacker News. The release marks a significant expansion of Wolfram's LLM integration into its scientific and engineering computation stack. Version 15 continues Wolfram's strategy of combining symbolic computation with neural approaches.


Mathematica v15 with native AI is a major update for scientific computing, engineering, and research workflows — directly relevant for technical teams using Wolfram tooling


Sources: Stephen Wolfram Blog / Hacker News


Technology


GrapheneOS Ported to Android 17 — Official Releases Coming Soon


Jun 16, 20:34


The GrapheneOS project announced it has successfully ported the privacy-hardened Android fork to Android 17, with official releases imminent, drawing 747 upvotes and 354 comments on Hacker News — one of the most-engaged tech stories of the day. The port means GrapheneOS users will gain access to Android 17's new features without sacrificing the project's hardened security posture. Android 17 launched to Pixel devices earlier this week, making the quick turnaround notable.


The fastest-growing privacy-focused Android distribution maintaining parity with the latest platform release matters for security-conscious enterprises and individuals deploying hardened mobile devices


Sources: GrapheneOS / Hacker News


Tesco Sprinting to Exit VMware/Broadcom Despite Migration Risks — Court Date Set for Licensing Dispute


Jun 17, 07:30


UK retail giant Tesco has accelerated its departure from VMware following Broadcom's acquisition, turning to third-party support as a court sets a date to hear the licensing dispute between the two companies. Tesco's aggressive exit timeline reflects the broader enterprise backlash against Broadcom's VMware pricing changes. The case is being closely watched as a test of how large enterprises can legally navigate forced migrations from VMware licensing terms.


Tesco's court battle and emergency migration is the highest-profile test case for the wave of enterprises seeking to escape Broadcom's VMware pricing — outcome will influence strategy for thousands of organizations


Sources: The Register


AMD Acquires Mext to Address AI-Created RAM Shortage with Flash-Based Memory Expansion


Jun 16, 22:09


AMD acquired Mext, a company developing AI-driven flash-based memory expansion technology, in a move analysts describe as AMD using AI to solve the memory shortage that AI demand itself created. The acquisition adds a software-defined memory tier that treats fast flash storage as an extension of DRAM, potentially easing the HBM and DRAM supply crunch hitting AI infrastructure builders. The deal positions AMD to offer a fuller-stack solution for memory-constrained AI workloads.


A hardware solution to the AI-driven DRAM shortage from a major CPU/GPU vendor has direct implications for data center infrastructure planning and AI compute cost trajectories


Sources: The Register


Databricks Announces Lakehouse//RT and LTAP at Data+AI Summit — Claims to Solve Decades-Old Pipeline Problem for AI Agents


Jun 16, 20:04


Databricks announced two products at its Data + AI Summit: Lakehouse//RT, delivering millisecond query latency directly on governed Delta/Iceberg tables, and LTAP (Lake Transactional/Analytical Processing), which stores Postgres-native transactional data in Delta/Iceberg format from the point of write — eliminating the ETL pipelines that have connected operational and analytical systems for decades. Co-founder Reynold Xin described a simpler stack as 'the holy grail for agents,' arguing AI agents need infrastructure out of the way to move fast. The announcements directly target the latency and complexity gaps that have blocked real-time agentic AI deployments.


Eliminating the ETL layer between transactional and analytical data is a structural change to the data infrastructure underpinning every AI agent deployment — relevant for every data engineering and AI platform team


Sources: VentureBeat


Stop Killing Games Initiative Fails to Secure EU Legislation Despite 1.3 Million Signatures


Jun 17, 01:40


The Stop Killing Games campaign, which gathered 1.3 million signatures across Europe calling for legislation requiring publishers to keep online games playable after official support ends, failed to secure EU legislative action. The European Citizens' Initiative process requires follow-up from the European Commission, which declined to pursue formal legislation. The outcome is a setback for digital consumer rights advocates who argued game shutdowns destroy purchased software permanently.


The failure to translate 1.3M signatures into EU law on digital product longevity signals the limits of citizen initiatives against platform-era business models — relevant for digital rights and software licensing policy


Sources: Dexerto / Hacker News


Apple Plans to Move Hide My Email to New Domain — Privacy Experts Warn It Could Reduce Effectiveness


Jun 16, 22:09


Apple is preparing to migrate its Hide My Email anonymized address feature to a different domain in coming weeks, a change privacy experts say could reduce its effectiveness as spam filters and services adapt. The move is unannounced to users and affects a privacy feature relied upon by iCloud+ subscribers to mask their real email addresses. The technical change has drawn concern from privacy advocates about whether the new domain will maintain the same trusted status.


A quiet change to a widely used Apple privacy feature that may degrade its effectiveness is directly relevant to users and enterprises relying on it for email privacy and security


Sources: TechCrunch


Business & Markets


SpaceX Briefly Passes Microsoft to Become World's Fourth Most Valuable Company


Jun 17, 09:13


SpaceX's stock surged further in its third day of public trading, briefly eclipsing Microsoft to become the world's fourth most valuable listed company before settling as the fifth, overtaking Amazon, with a market cap around $2.6–2.7 trillion. The company's valuation has grown by roughly $1 trillion since trading began Friday. Elon Musk is now the world's first trillionaire.


SpaceX's ascent to the top tier of global market cap reshapes competitive dynamics across AI, cloud, defense, and developer tools — its Cursor acquisition makes it a direct enterprise software competitor


Sources: Euronews Business · TechCrunch · NYT


Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady at Kevin Warsh's First Meeting as Chair


Jun 17, 09:05


The Federal Reserve is widely expected to hold interest rates steady at Kevin Warsh's debut policy meeting as chair, with markets watching closely for signals on his rate trajectory and how he'll navigate post-Iran War inflation alongside the White House's preference for cuts. Warsh faces a complex first meeting: inflation remains elevated from energy disruption, the economy is absorbing supply chain restructuring, and the Fed's independence is under unusual political scrutiny. His communication tone will set market expectations for the remainder of 2026.


Fed rate direction under new, politically contentious leadership directly affects technology borrowing costs, startup financing conditions, and enterprise capital planning for the rest of the year


Sources: NYT · NYT DealBook


China Restricts Citizens from Engaging with Global Capital Markets to Keep Money at Home


Jun 16, 23:00


Beijing is imposing new restrictions limiting the ways individual Chinese investors can access global markets, in a deliberate effort to keep domestic capital within China's borders as the post-war economy faces household spending weakness. The restrictions come alongside already-reported declines in retail sales and reflect structural concerns about capital flight. The move signals China is increasingly prioritizing domestic capital retention over financial market liberalization.


Capital controls targeting Chinese retail investors affect global markets, multinational revenue exposure in China, and the investment landscape for tech companies operating in or targeting Chinese markets


Sources: NYT


Ireland Takes EU Council Presidency July 1 — Tech Regulation and Big Tech Accountability Are Central Agenda Items


Jun 17, 07:30


Ireland assumes the rotating EU Council Presidency on July 1, with tech regulation forming a major part of its agenda — a significant tension given that Ireland hosts the European headquarters of Google, Meta, Apple, and most other major U.S. tech companies. Politico's coverage across multiple pieces highlights that Dublin must broker fierce budget negotiations, navigate cybersecurity and hybrid threat policy, and shape Big Tech compliance decisions while being those companies' primary EU regulator. The presidency also runs into France's election cycle, narrowing the legislative window.


The country that houses the EU offices of virtually every major U.S. tech company taking over EU regulatory agenda-setting creates a direct conflict of interest with live implications for AI regulation, DSA enforcement, and data privacy


Sources: Politico EU · Politico EU


Australian Sugar Producer Mackay Sugar Hit by Cyberattack During Peak Cane Crushing Season


Jun 17, 02:16


Mackay Sugar, one of Australia's largest sugar producers, suffered a cyberattack that has forced crops to remain in the ground during peak cane crushing season — directly disrupting the harvest window that determines annual yield. The attack demonstrates the cascading operational impact when cyber incidents hit industrial and agricultural businesses at the worst possible time. Details on the attacker and attack type have not been disclosed.


Cyberattacks timed to disrupt industrial and agricultural operations at critical seasonal windows represent an emerging class of high-impact attacks beyond traditional IT environments


Sources: The Register

Steam Workshop Abused to Distribute Malware Hidden in Wallpaper Engine Packages


Jun 16, 24:00


Threat actors are hiding malware inside wallpaper packages uploaded to Steam Workshop, exploiting the trusted distribution channel of Valve's Wallpaper Engine app to push payloads to users. The attack abuses community-sourced content infrastructure — users installing what appear to be legitimate wallpapers are silently executing malware. This follows a broader pattern of attackers abusing trusted platform ecosystems (AUR, WordPress CDN) for malware distribution.


Gaming platform supply chain attacks targeting widely installed consumer apps represent a new distribution vector that bypasses traditional enterprise content controls


Sources: BleepingComputer


FIFA World Cup Internal System Bug Would Have Let Anyone Modify Live TV Streams
